samples.summary: Collapsed-caret keyboard toggle now layers named-style defaults (`effectiveVisual`) — no test covers that branch
samples.evidence: `toggleStyle` changed from `!visual[key]` to `!(inRange ?? !!effectiveVisual[key])`. `isStyleOnInSelection` returns `undefined` when there is no selection, so the *only* thing exercising the new `styleDefaultsAtCursor()` layer is the collapsed-caret path (Cmd+I with the caret inside a Heading 6 should stage `italic:false` in the pending style). Every new engine test that touches heading-6 (packages/docs/test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts:242 `selectAll`, :258 'Cmd+I removes the style-provided italic') creates a real range first, so it goes through `isStyleOnInSelection` and would pass even if `effectiveVisual` were reverted to `visual`. No test in test/view/pending-style*.test.ts uses a heading block at all (grep for `headingLevel` in pending-style-integration.test.ts: 0 hits).
searchedFor: grep headingLevel in packages/docs/test/view (7 files, none of them pending-style*)

samples.summary: The stated 'pending/stored style stays raw' invariant (defaults must not be baked into a run) has no test
samples.evidence: The diff deliberately splits `caretStyle(false)` (raw, used as the *stored* `base` for the pending style) from `caretStyle(true)` (effective, used for reads), and the comments claim baking a default into a stored run 'would break the lazy cascade when the named style is later redefined'. The same split exists in text-editor.ts (`visual` raw vs `effectiveVisual`). No test asserts that after a collapsed-caret step/toggle inside a named-styled block the stored pending style — or the run typed afterwards — contains only the explicit keys and not the named-style defaults (fontSize/color/italic of heading-6). Since `getSelectionStyle()` now returns the effective style, a regression that stored the effective style would be invisible: all new assertions (text-box-editor.test.ts new describe, backward-selection-toggle.test.ts) only read effective values.
searchedFor: grep pending in packages/docs/test/view (15 files) and inspected pending-style-editor.test.ts / pending-style-integration.test.ts for heading blocks

samples.summary: Text-box collapsed-caret font-size step from the named-style default is untested (only the range path is)
samples.evidence: `stepSelectionFontSize`'s no-selection branch changed to read `current` from `effective = {...caretStyle(true), ...staged}` instead of the raw run (previously falling back to 11). The new test 'steps the font size from the named-style default, not the 11pt fallback' (packages/docs/test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts, in the new describe) calls `selectAll(...)` first, so it exercises the *range* branch through `visitStyledRunsInRange`, not the collapsed-caret branch. The pre-existing collapsed-caret test (text-box-editor.test.ts:786) uses a paragraph with an explicit `fontSize: 11`, so it passes with either the raw or the effective read.

samples.summary: New index clamping in `visitCellRectangleSlices` (stale/out-of-range cell rectangle) has no test
samples.evidence: Lines 51-59 add clamping of minRow/maxRow/minCol/maxCol to the table's own dimensions, described as protecting against 'a stale or malformed cell range'. Every cell-rectangle test in the diff (packages/docs/test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts:535 and :558) uses an in-bounds 1x2 rectangle, so the clamp arms are never taken; removing the clamping entirely would keep all tests green (the old `rows[r]?.cells[c]` guard already made out-of-range harmless). There is also no dedicated test file for the new modules (no packages/docs/test/model/range-slices.test.ts or range-runs.test.ts).
searchedFor: grep visitCellRectangleSlices|visitRangeSlices|visitStyledRunsInRange across repo — only src, backward-selection-toggle.test.ts, table.test.ts and docs/*.md

samples.summary: `isStyleOnInSelection`'s 'range holds no text runs → fall back to the caret' branch is untested
samples.evidence: The function returns `undefined` when `sawRun` stays false (a real selection spanning only empty/zero-width blocks), which then falls back to `effectiveVisual`. No test in the new packages/docs/test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts (or elsewhere under test/view) creates a selection over empty blocks and presses Cmd+B; every scenario there has text in every covered block, so the `sawRun === false` path never runs.

samples.summary: Test titled 'reports the same value at a collapsed caret as over the range' never creates a range
samples.evidence: The test calls `mountHeading6()` and immediately asserts `getRangeStyleSummary().italic` and `getSelectionStyle().italic` without selecting anything, so `getRangeStyleSummary()` takes its no-selection (caret) branch. Both assertions exercise the same caret code path; the 'as over the range' half of the claim is not tested here (it is tested separately by the selectAll tests above).

samples.summary: Slim header/footer toggles' pressed state is not covered (and is not wired to the summary at all)
samples.evidence: The sibling suites for TextFormatGroup and the slides mobile bar assert `aria-pressed` follows the range summary (tests/components/text-formatting/text-format-toggles.test.ts, tests/app/slides/toolbar/mobile-text-toggles.test.ts). The new header/footer suite only asserts `applyStyle` arguments; the slim toolbar's `<Toggle>`s (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:449/458/467) carry no `pressed` prop, so their visual state is uncontrolled and no test pins it either way.

verdict.reason: The new `effectiveVisual = { ...styleDefaultsAtCursor(), ...visual }` layer in `toggleStyle` (text-editor.ts:2898, used at :2906-2908) is only consulted when `isStyleOnInSelection` returns undefined (text-editor.ts:3011-3023), i.e. the collapsed-caret / run-less-range fallback that writes the pending style (:2918). `toggleStyle` is reachable only from the keyboard shortcut handlers (text-editor.ts:874-904). Only four docs test files simulate modifier keydowns (grep `metaKey`/`ctrlKey` under packages/docs): backward-selection-toggle.test.ts, pending-style-editor.test.ts, text-box-editor.test.ts, editor-read-only.test.ts. The heading-6 suite in backward-selection-toggle.test.ts:220-282 always builds a real range via selectAll (:242) over the run "abcd", so those assertions (:253, :266, :279) pass identically with plain `visual`. The only collapsed-caret keyboard toggles (pending-style-editor.test.ts:132-174) use createEmptyBlock() — a paragraph whose `normal-text` style has no boolean inline defaults (named-styles.ts:87-91 shows heading-6 is the only built-in with `italic: true`), so it cannot distinguish the layer either. text-box-editor.test.ts:834-958 does use heading-6 but only asserts getRangeStyleSummary/getSelectionStyle and dispatches only Cmd+A (:902), never a style shortcut. pending-style*.test.ts drive the controller directly with no heading/styled block. No counterexample found: the changed collapsed-caret + named-style-default branch has no discriminating test.

finding.summary: Text-box `getRangeStyleSummary` behavior change (raw run style → effective style with named-style defaults) has no test
finding.evidence: The diff replaces the text-box summary walk so each key is read from the *effective* style (`{...namedStyleDefaults, ...inline.style}`) instead of raw `inline.style`, and its comment claims this fixes the toolbar answering "not italic" for a run painted italic by its named style (heading-6 sets `italic: true`, packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:91). I found no test asserting this for text boxes: packages/docs/test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts only touches getRangeStyleSummary for fontSize/pending-style stepping (lines ~809-816), and the slides consumer stubs it out entirely (packages/slides/test/view/editor/text-box-editor.test.ts:82 `getRangeStyleSummary: () => ({})`). The new packages/docs/test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts exercises only `initialize` (the docs editor), never `initializeTextBox`. So the docs/slides text-box + shape + table-cell editors' summary change (and its knock-on effect on fontSize/color reported from title/heading blocks) can break without any test failing.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the text-box `getRangeStyleSummary` effective-style change has no test. It does: packages/docs/test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts:834-958 is a dedicated describe block, 'initializeTextBox — named-style defaults in the style reads', that the reviewer missed by stopping at line ~818. It mounts a real `initializeTextBox` over a heading-6 block whose run carries no explicit style (test:872-894), drives a real range via Cmd/Ctrl+A on the hidden textarea (test:897-906), and asserts `getRangeStyleSummary().italic === true`, `.fontSize === 11`, `.color === '#666666'` (test:911-913) — values supplied ONLY by the heading-6 named style (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:91). Under the old raw-`inline.style` walk those reads would be undefined, so the assertions are non-vacuous and would fail on regression. It further covers explicit-run-style precedence (test:917-923), the collapsed-caret branch parity that the changed code at packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1011-1013 implements (test:925-932), and the fontSize knock-on via stepSelectionFontSize from a heading-1 default 20→21 (test:934-957). Nothing under test is mocked away: the changed walk `visitStyledRunsInRange` at packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1049 is the real code path. The slides stub (`getRangeStyleSummary: () => ({})`) is irrelevant because the behavior lives in the docs factory that slides consumes, and that factory is covered here.
